title: Python Data Types
learningObjectives: Explain that every Python value is an object with a type.
Recognize common built-in numeric, text, Boolean and collection types.
Use type() and isinstance() to inspect values.
Distinguish mutable and immutable built-in objects at an introductory level.
Choose a suitable data type for a simple programming task.

understand.concept: A data type describes the kind of value an object represents and the operations that make sense for it. Python includes numeric types such as int and float, text values such as str, Boolean values such as bool, and collection types such as list, tuple, set and dict. The built-in type() function reports an object's type; isinstance() checks whether an object belongs to a type or its subclass. Some objects are mutable and can be changed in place, while immutable objects cannot be changed after creation.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing appropriate types makes data easier to validate, process and communicate. Understanding mutability helps avoid unexpected changes when objects are shared between names or functions.
understand.analogy: A data type is like a label on a storage container that tells you what kind of item it is designed to hold and what operations are sensible.
understand.analogyLimit: Python variables do not permanently lock a value into a container of one type. A name can be rebound to a different object, and Python's type system has more nuance than a physical label.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Common built-in types

Python's built-in types include `int` for integers, `float` for floating-point numbers, `complex` for complex numbers, `str` for text, `bool` for truth values and `NoneType` for the special value `None`. Common collections include `list`, `tuple`, `set` and `dict`.

## 2. Inspect a value

Use `type(value)` to obtain its type. Use `isinstance(value, SomeType)` when checking whether a value is compatible with a type. In application code, prefer behaviour-oriented design where possible rather than scattering unnecessary type checks.

## 3. Mutable and immutable objects

Lists, dictionaries and sets are mutable: their contents can change. Integers, floats, strings and tuples are immutable: an existing object cannot be changed in place. Rebinding a name is not the same as mutating an object. A tuple can contain a mutable object, so immutability of the tuple does not make every nested object immutable.

## 4. Choose types deliberately

Use strings for text, numeric types for arithmetic, Booleans for true/false state, lists for ordered mutable sequences, tuples for fixed sequences, sets for unique elements and dictionaries for key-value associations. Later lessons explore each collection in depth.

examples.title: Inspect an integer
examples.explanation: The value is an integer object, so its type name is int.

examples.title: Inspect text and Boolean values
examples.explanation: Quoted text creates a string. True is a Boolean literal.

examples.title: Check a type with isinstance()
examples.explanation: isinstance() returns a Boolean indicating whether the object is an instance of the requested type.

examples.title: Observe list mutability
examples.explanation: append() mutates the existing list by adding an item.

examples.title: Observe string immutability
examples.explanation: upper() returns a new string. The name word is rebound to that new string; the original string is not modified.

practise.guidedTask: Create one value of type int, float, str, bool, list and dict. Print each value's type name, then mutate the list and compare the result.
practise.independentTask: Model a simple learner record using a string name, integer age, Boolean enrollment flag and list of completed topics. Inspect the types and add one topic to the list.
hints: Use type(value).__name__ for a readable type name.
Use isinstance(value, int) to check compatibility with int.
Lists and dictionaries can be changed in place.
A name can be rebound to a different object without changing the old object.
practise.challenge: Write a function that accepts a value and reports whether it is text, numeric or a list. Explain why isinstance() can be preferable to comparing type names directly.

questions.explanation: str is Python's built-in text sequence type.

questions.prompt: Which function checks whether an object is an instance of a type?
questions.explanation: isinstance(value, type) performs an instance check and also accounts for subclass relationships.
A list can be changed in place, for example by appending or removing elements.
A decimal floating-point literal such as 3.5 creates a float object.

questions.prompt: What happens when a name is rebound from one string to another?
options: The name refers to the new string object
The original string is edited in place
questions.answer: The name refers to the new string object
questions.explanation: Strings are immutable; assignment changes the name's binding rather than modifying the original string.
